content:
Kevin Osei: Dropping the latest ABM security FAQ addenda drafts here for Security/GRC review before PMM locks copy. FinServ + Healthcare versions. Main deltas are retention/residency + audit log language.
Links:
- FinServ addendum (Drive): https://drive.google.com/.../finserv-security-faq-addendum
- Healthcare addendum (Drive): https://drive.google.com/.../healthcare-security-faq-addendum
Would love redlines esp on: (1) “we don’t store prompts/outputs” phrasing, (2) audit log retention/export, (3) what evidence we can share pre-NDA.

Dr. Aisha Rahman: thx Kevin. Quick pass: we need to be tighter on “don’t store” + avoid absolutes.
In both docs, please replace any version of “Redwood does not store prompts or outputs” with something like:
“By default, Redwood does not retain customer prompts/outputs beyond what is necessary to provide the service and maintain reliability (e.g., transient processing and limited operational telemetry). Retention controls vary by deployment mode and can be configured for regulated use cases.”
Also remove “HIPAA compliant” from Healthcare. We can say “supports HIPAA-regulated workloads” / “can support a BAA (subject to review)” but Legal wants exact wording.

Soojin Lee: Got it. On the landing page we currently have a line “No prompt retention.” Sounds like we should soften that to match. Kevin can you paste the approved sentence here once finalized so Marketing uses same block across assets?

Olga Petrov: +1 on absolutes. Also: audit logs section in FinServ addendum says “audit logs retained for 1 year.” That’s not universally true today.
We should say:
- “Audit logs are available”
- “Retention period depends on deployment and configured export/retention in customer-controlled system”
If we have a default retention in Hosted vs Private, we should state it explicitly *only if it’s in the current control set and documented*.

Marcus Lin: I’m looking at the audit logging Q&A:
Current: “All customer actions and all API requests are logged and can be streamed to your SIEM.”
That’s too broad. We log admin/control-plane actions; request-level logging is configurable and for regulated we typically recommend export of relevant events.
Suggest:
“Redwood provides audit logs for administrative actions in the console/control plane (e.g., user/auth changes, key configuration changes, policy updates). For Private deployments, customers can integrate logs with their centralized logging/SIEM pipelines. Request/response payload logging is not enabled by default and can be controlled based on data sensitivity.”
Also, call it “log export” not “streamed” unless we actually have streaming integration GA.

Markus Klein: From SE side: prospects keep asking “can you send audit logs to Splunk?” We’ve been saying “we can export to S3 and you can ingest to Splunk.”
Maybe we add a single line: “Common pattern: export to customer S3 + SIEM ingestion (Splunk/Datadog/etc.)” without saying we have a native Splunk app.

Fatima Noor: +1. Also want to avoid “we’ll complete any security questionnaire in 48 hours” (FinServ addendum says that). We can say “we prioritize regulated security reviews and can typically turn initial responses quickly” but don’t commit SLA in a PDF.

Camila Reyes: Agree on the questionnaire SLA. Let’s keep it as “fast turnaround with Security/GRC support” and route specifics via SE.
Question: what can we include about SOC 2 and pen test? We have a slide that says “SOC2 Type II.” Is it ok to say “available under NDA”?

Dr. Aisha Rahman: SOC 2: ok to say “SOC 2 Type II report available under NDA.”
Pen test: do NOT say “pen test report available” broadly. We can offer “executive summary available under NDA” case-by-case. If asked, we can share via the Trust portal workflow.
Also, do not list specific controls as “certified” unless it’s part of the SOC scope.

Olga Petrov: +1. Add “security package available upon request (NDA may be required)” is fine. Avoid enumerating detailed findings/remediation timelines.
For Healthcare doc: BAA language needs to be exact (Sofia, can you weigh in?).

Sofia Mendes: Please avoid “we sign BAAs for all customers.” Replace with:
“Redwood can enter into a Business Associate Agreement (BAA) for eligible customers and deployment modes, subject to legal and security review.”
Also please remove “HIPAA compliant” as Aisha said. We can say “designed to support HIPAA-regulated workflows” but that’s still squishy—prefer “can support HIPAA-regulated workloads.”

Kevin Osei: Super helpful. Summarizing proposed edits for both addenda:
1) Replace “no prompt retention” / “we do not store prompts/outputs” with the “by default, does not retain beyond necessary…” wording (Aisha’s sentence).
2) Audit logs:
- Narrow to admin/control-plane audit events
- Remove “all API requests are logged” claim
- Replace “streamed to SIEM” with “export/integrate with customer logging/SIEM pipeline”
- Remove fixed “1 year retention” and make it “depends on deployment + customer export/retention”
3) Evidence:
- “SOC2 Type II available under NDA” OK
- “Pen test exec summary may be available under NDA” only
- Security package language ok
4) Remove questionnaire turnaround commitments
5) Healthcare: replace BAA/HIPAA wording per Sofia

I’ll push an updated draft in ~1 hour for final thumbs.

Marcus Lin: One more nit: KMS/HSM language.
Healthcare addendum currently: “Supports customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM.”
We should say:
“Supports integration with customer key management services (e.g., cloud KMS) for encryption key control in Private/VPC deployments; HSM support depends on customer environment and integration approach.”
We’ve had prospects interpret this as “we ship an HSM.”

Markus Klein: Yes please. We’ve been answering “we can integrate with your KMS; if you’re using HSM-backed KMS that’s on your side.”

Soojin Lee: Can we get a single approved block for: retention + audit logs + evidence share? I’ll put that into the PMM “approved language” sheet and the email sequence copy.

Dr. Aisha Rahman: Here’s an approved starting point for retention (fine to reuse verbatim):
“By default, Redwood does not retain customer prompts/outputs beyond what is necessary to provide the service and maintain reliability (e.g., transient processing and limited operational telemetry). For regulated workloads, we recommend Dedicated or Private deployment modes and can align retention and logging configurations to your security requirements.”
For evidence:
“Security documentation (including our SOC 2 Type II report) is available upon request; NDA may be required.”
For audit logs:
“Redwood provides audit logs for administrative/control-plane actions. For Private deployments, audit logs can be exported into customer-controlled logging/SIEM systems as part of the reference architecture.”

Olga Petrov: On retention: let’s avoid “limited operational telemetry” if we can’t explain it. But if we keep it, add “does not include prompt/output content by default” OR remove the parenthetical.
Maybe:
“…beyond what is necessary to provide the service (transient processing) and operate the platform (service metadata and security events).”

Kevin Osei: Makes sense. I’ll revise the parenthetical to “service metadata + security events” and avoid implying content retention.

Camila Reyes: Great. Once updated draft is in, can Security react with :white_check_mark: in-thread so we can move to publishing? We’re trying to hit final approval by EOD.

Kevin Osei: Updated drafts uploaded (same links). Key changes:
- Retention language updated per Aisha + Olga
- Audit logging narrowed per Marcus
- Evidence share language updated per Aisha
- Removed questionnaire turnaround line
- Healthcare BAA/HIPAA wording per Sofia
- KMS/HSM line clarified
Can I get final sign-off?

Dr. Aisha Rahman: Reviewed. Looks good from Security. :white_check_mark: Only request: in FinServ addendum, change “guarantees data residency” to “supports regional deployment options; residency depends on selected region/deployment and customer configuration.”

Olga Petrov: +1. Otherwise GRC ok. :white_check_mark:

Marcus Lin: :white_check_mark: from SecEng. Thanks for tightening the audit log scope.

Sofia Mendes: Legal ok with the BAA language as written. :white_check_mark:

Soojin Lee: Perfect. I’ll sync these exact blocks into the landing page + outbound copy and note “no absolutes” in the messaging doc.

Camila Reyes: Awesome, thanks all. Kevin, please paste the final approved retention/audit/evidence blocks into the #marketing thread too so we don’t drift.

Kevin Osei: Will do. Posting approved blocks now + updating the internal “security FAQ language” snippet library.
